hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=-\dfrac{7}{3}x$

This line goes through two of the opposite corner points $(-3, 7)$, and $(3,-7)$.

Under this transformation, each point on the hexagon maps to another point which is also on the hexagon. The hexagon is *symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A hexagon mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center is at the origin. The hexagon has a point around negative eight, one, a point around eight, negative  one, a point around negative three, nine, a point around three, negative seven, a point around five, six, and a point around negative five, negative six. The equation y equals negative seven over three X is graphed on the coordinate plane. All points are estimates. The hexagon is reflected about the line, and all the points map to other points from the pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $x$-axis

Under this transformation, some points on the hexagon map to another point which is no longer on the hexagon. The hexagon is *not symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A hexagon mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center is at the origin. The hexagon has a point around negative eight, one, a point around eight, negative  one, a point around negative three, nine, a point around three, negative seven, a point around five, six, and a point around negative five, negative six. All points are estimates. The hexagon is reflected about the x axis with dotted lines showing where the points of the image hexagon would be after the reflection. The endpoints of the dotted lines are outside the current pre-image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the hexagon are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=-\dfrac{7}{3}x$ | Yes
Reflective symmetry over the $x$-axis | No
